# Cinnamon

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="cinnamon-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="cinnamon-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="cinnamon-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Lead is the metal to check in cinnamon: about one in eight monitoring results exceeds the EU limit of 2,000 µg/kg, and adulteration with lead chromate caused a 2023 outbreak.<sup <ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Lead first, then chromium and cadmium; aluminium is high but unregulated, and arsenic and mercury are usually low.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Soil and dust on the bark, form and species label, and deliberate adulteration with lead chromate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" </li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot-specific lead and chromium results, with species and form recorded.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">LHAAC · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Coordinated Sampling Project 41: Microbial and Heavy Metal Detections in Herbs and Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Local Health Authorities Analytical Committee, Edith Cowan University</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="cinnamon-overview"></a>
<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Cinnamon overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Lead is the metal that decides most cinnamon questions. In 808 WHO GEMS/Food lead results for cinnamon bark from 2003 to 2024, the median was about 350 µg/kg and 103 results (13%) were above 2,000 µg/kg, the EU maximum for bark spices.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Codex set a 2,500 µg/kg lead limit for dried bark spices in 2025, and China allows 3,000 µg/kg for cassia bark.<sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite">[[sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">National Health Commission, State Administration for Market Regulation · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants">GB 2762-2025: National Food Safety Standard — Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Retail surveys show the same wide spread. Ten powdered products bought in Queensland ranged from 150 to 7,000 µg/kg lead, 37 bulk samples from Casablanca averaged 2,050 µg/kg, and five cassia samples from Iraq averaged 4,159 µg/kg, while single samples from Indonesia and Serbia held 23 and 310 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span A separate problem is deliberate adulteration. In 2023 cinnamon ground in Ecuador and contaminated with lead chromate reached the United States in apple cinnamon pouches that held 1,900–5,800 µg/kg lead as sold, and 566 cases of elevated blood lead were reported in 44 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Napier MD, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Childhood Lead Exposure Linked to Apple Cinnamon Fruit Puree Pouches — North Carolina, June 2023–January 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Those results are kept apart from the ordinary occurrence data on this page. <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-cinnamon" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-cinnamon-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one subgroup and metal; a mean, median and range from the same samples are separate rows. Cassia, Ceylon (<i>C. verum</i>) and cinnamon of unstated species are labelled separately, as are ground and whole forms. Ratings place a reported mean, median or sample result against a pooled HMI cinnamon reference built from every compatible sampling family. Same-study contrasts compare a subgroup with its own study’s total or lowest subgroup. Rows from the 2023–2024 applesauce outbreak measure the finished food, not cinnamon, and are not rated. Held rows failed a check against their own paper and are shown but not compared.</p>

Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:cinnamon-pooled-Pb:a45b95d60100"><summary>HMI cinnamon Pb reference · 7 sampling families</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:cinnamon-pooled-Pb:a45b95d60100"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI cinnamon Pb reference · 7 sampling families. Dried cinnamon bark as sold or analysed, µg/kg; dry-weight and as-is labels pooled. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>212</td><td>310</td><td>800</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>193–200 (bounded)</td><td>310</td><td>800</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>94 reference units; 7 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>75</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Bua et al. 2016</td><td>2</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Cicero et al. 2022</td><td>1</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Moussa et al. 2024</td><td>8</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Savić et al. 2019</td><td>1</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Tinggi et al. 2025</td><td>6</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Ammar et al. 2023</td><td>1</td><td>14%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians from every compatible cinnamon sampling family in the evidence ledger: WHO GEMS/Food medians by reporting region, year, labelled species and form (random sampling only), per-product results printed by individual surveys, and published subgroup medians. Each family has equal total weight; subgroups have equal weight within a family. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations, and outbreak or adulteration samples never enter.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1–Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>An international evidence-library reference for dried cinnamon of all species, not a probability sample of the world market and not a Cassia-only or Ceylon-only reference. GEMS/Food regions are reporting regions, not growing origins. Dry-weight and as-is results are pooled because both describe a dried spice whose residual moisture is not reported. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy" class="internal" data-slug="sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy" data-no-cite-meta>Bua et al. 2016</a></li><li><a href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs" class="internal" data-slug="sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs" data-no-cite-meta>Cicero et al. 2022</a></li><li><a href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon" class="internal" data-slug="sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon" data-no-cite-meta>Moussa et al. 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/savic2019-serbian-spices-minerals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/savic2019-serbian-spices-minerals" data-no-cite-meta>Savić et al. 2019</a></li><li><a href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland" class="internal" data-slug="sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland" data-no-cite-meta>Tinggi et al. 2025</a></li><li><a href="../sources/ammar2023-element-migration-aluminum-cookware" class="internal" data-slug="sources/ammar2023-element-migration-aluminum-cookware" data-no-cite-meta>Ammar et al. 2023</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Any basis conversion used for its HMI comparison is stated separately with the numerical target.</p></details><p><a href="https://doi.org/10.3390/foods11040548">Open the primary publication</a> · <a href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs" class="internal" data-slug="sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs">HMI source record</a></p></div></div></div><p class="hmi-explorer-empty" data-explorer-empty hidden>No findings match these filters. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach cinnamon

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

Cinnamon carries metals from two very different routes. The ordinary route is the bark and what settles on it: nearly every product carries measurable lead, cadmium, nickel, chromium and aluminium, consistent with uptake from soil and with dust.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Iraq, unwashed spices held on average 7% more lead and 14% more cadmium than the same spices washed, a sign that part of the burden sits on the surface.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

The second route is adulteration. The United States Food and Drug Administration traced the 2023 applesauce lead to cinnamon ground in Ecuador and reported that the lead and chromium came from lead chromate, a yellow pigment.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Napier MD, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Childhood Lead Exposure Linked to Apple Cinnamon Fruit Puree Pouches — North Carolina, June 2023–January 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Lead chromate raises lead and chromium together, so the two are screened as a pair; a Western Australian survey of 380 products found no evidence of high lead chromate in the samples it screened.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">LHAAC · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Coordinated Sampling Project 41: Microbial and Heavy Metal Detections in Herbs and Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Local Health Authorities Analytical Committee, Edith Cowan University</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Equipment and grinding are plausible third routes. Australian authors suggest that aluminium utensils and stainless-steel equipment may add aluminium, chromium and nickel; the Vietnamese product with 7,000 µg/kg lead also carried 920,000 µg/kg aluminium, 4,000 µg/kg chromium and 2,000 µg/kg nickel.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study in the ledger measured cinnamon before and after grinding.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which cinnamon types and origins measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

For lead, cinnamon labelled as Ceylon (C. verum) measured lower than cinnamon labelled as cassia in the largest dataset.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In WHO GEMS/Food, 58 lead results labelled C. verum had a median of 225 µg/kg, with 2 (3%) above 2,000 µg/kg, against a median of 392 µg/kg and 60 of 268 (22%) above 2,000 µg/kg for results labelled cassia.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most cassia results came from one Western Pacific reporting region, so species and source cannot be separated, and the labels were not verified.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Within single studies, the C. verum label did not guarantee low lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bua DG, Annuario G, Albergamo A, Cicero N, Dugo G · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy">Heavy metals in aromatic spices by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Queensland products labelled C. verum ranged from 150 µg/kg (China) and 160 µg/kg (Vietnam) to 2,400 µg/kg (Sri Lanka), 2,500 µg/kg (India) and 7,000 µg/kg (Vietnam).<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Three C. verum samples on the Italian market measured 294 µg/kg (Madagascar) and 766 µg/kg (Indonesia), while the Vietnamese sample was higher but its printed mean conflicts with its own replicate range.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bua DG, Annuario G, Albergamo A, Cicero N, Dugo G · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy">Heavy metals in aromatic spices by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bua2016-aromatic-spices-metals-italy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are lowest observed values from one to two samples per country, not a ranking of countries.

Form mattered more consistently for lead. Sticks and pieces in GEMS/Food had a median of 90 µg/kg and none of 46 results above 2,000 µg/kg, against a median of 560 µg/kg and 20 of 234 above it for ground cinnamon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Western Australia found that most lead results above 2,000 µg/kg were ground cinnamon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">LHAAC · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Coordinated Sampling Project 41: Microbial and Heavy Metal Detections in Herbs and Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Local Health Authorities Analytical Committee, Edith Cowan University</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> This is a tentative pattern: the sticks came from fewer regions and years.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Cadmium follows species and origin less clearly. GEMS/Food cadmium had a median of about 220 µg/kg with no result above 1,000 µg/kg, and C. verum-labelled results were somewhat lower (median 150 against 230 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> One Sri Lankan product in Queensland reached 3,700 µg/kg while the other held 150 µg/kg, and five Iraqi cassia samples averaged 874 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Choosing sticks for lead can raise chromium. In the one GEMS/Food submission that measured chromium, five stick samples had a median of 760 µg/kg against 215 µg/kg for ten ground samples.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Arsenic and mercury are low enough in most cinnamon that their comparisons rarely change a decision: GEMS/Food total mercury never exceeded 50 µg/kg and inorganic arsenic was 27 µg/kg at most.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-ceylon-cinnamon-lower-in-lead-than-cassia" data-anchor="is-ceylon-cinnamon-lower-in-lead-than-cassia" data-question="Is Ceylon cinnamon lower in lead than cassia?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is Ceylon cinnamon lower in lead than cassia?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the monitoring data, yes on average: GEMS/Food results labelled C. verum had a median of 225 µg/kg lead against 392 µg/kg for cassia-labelled results, and far fewer exceeded 2,000 µg/kg (3% against 22%).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> But the labels were not verified, most cassia results came from one reporting region, and Australian products labelled C. verum ranged up to 7,000 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-cinnamon-sticks-lower-in-metals-than-ground-cinnamon" data-anchor="are-cinnamon-sticks-lower-in-metals-than-ground-cinnamon" data-question="Are cinnamon sticks lower in metals than ground cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are cinnamon sticks lower in metals than ground cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, yes in the monitoring data: sticks had a median of 90 µg/kg and none of 46 results above 2,000 µg/kg, against 560 µg/kg for ground cinnamon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For chromium, the one submission measuring both forms found sticks higher (median 760 against 215 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>


<a id="processing-extracts-and-finished-foods"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Washing, processing and finished foods

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processing evidence for cinnamon is thin. Across 23 Iraqi spices, unwashed portions held on average 7% more lead, 14% more cadmium and 11% more mercury than portions washed with tap and deionised water; cinnamon was not reported separately and the unwashed values were not printed.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study measured roasting, sterilisation or extraction.

Finished foods carry the cinnamon’s metals into much larger servings. A baby-food manufacturer accepted nine cinnamon lots with 20–887 µg/kg lead and 117–345 µg/kg cadmium under an internal specification of 1,000 µg/kg, and another recalculated one lot to the finished food as consumed.<sup class="cite">[[sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Economic and Consumer Policy · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Baby Foods Are Tainted with Dangerous Levels of Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Staff Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In the outbreak, the adulterated cinnamon raised lead in the whole puree to 1,900–3,000 µg/kg in pouches from affected homes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Napier MD, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Childhood Lead Exposure Linked to Apple Cinnamon Fruit Puree Pouches — North Carolina, June 2023–January 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>



<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation from sourcing to recall

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Controls for cinnamon act at sourcing, at lot acceptance and at recall. The measured comparisons are observational: lower lead in sticks than in ground cinnamon and in C. verum-labelled than in cassia-labelled results, and higher lead exceedance in bulk than in packaged spices in Lebanon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Cinnamon FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cinnamon" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cinnamon" data-question="What heavy metals are found in cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Lead is the metal most often found at levels that matter, with a GEMS/Food median of about 350 µg/kg and 13% of results above the EU limit of 2,000 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cinnamon also carries cadmium (GEMS/Food median about 220 µg/kg), chromium, nickel and a great deal of aluminium; arsenic and mercury are usually low.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/sabri2025-moroccan-spices-casablanca-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sabri S, Sabri C, Salam MR, El Mellouli F, Lafram A, Khallouki H, Hassane YA, Kabine M · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sabri2025-moroccan-spices-casablanca-metals">Essential and Toxic Element Profiles in Selected Spices from Greater Casablanca, Morocco</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">World&#39;s Veterinary Journal 15(4): 863-881</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sabri2025-moroccan-spices-casablanca-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-cinnamon" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-cinnamon" data-question="How do heavy metals get into cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Mostly from soil and dust taken up or deposited on the bark, and in some lots from deliberate adulteration with lead chromate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The 2023 outbreak cinnamon was contaminated this way after grinding in Ecuador.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-organic-cinnamon-free-from-heavy-metals" data-anchor="is-organic-cinnamon-free-from-heavy-metals" data-question="Is organic cinnamon free from heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is organic cinnamon free from heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No source in the ledger compares organic and conventional cinnamon for metals. Organic-labelled lots tested by a baby-food manufacturer held 20–126 µg/kg lead and 117–225 µg/kg cadmium, so organic cinnamon is not metal-free.<sup class="cite">[[sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Economic and Consumer Policy · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Baby Foods Are Tainted with Dangerous Levels of Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Staff Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-type-of-cinnamon-has-the-lowest-lead" data-anchor="which-type-of-cinnamon-has-the-lowest-lead" data-question="Which type of cinnamon has the lowest lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which type of cinnamon has the lowest lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the monitoring data, whole sticks and cinnamon labelled C. verum (Ceylon) were lowest, with lead medians of 90 and 225 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Neither is a guarantee: Australian products labelled C. verum reached 7,000 µg/kg, and sticks were higher in chromium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-countries-produce-cinnamon-with-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-countries-produce-cinnamon-with-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which countries produce cinnamon with the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which countries produce cinnamon with the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The evidence cannot rank countries. Single samples from Indonesia measured 23 µg/kg lead in one study and 766 µg/kg in another, products from Vietnam and Sri Lanka ranged from 160 to 7,000 µg/kg within one survey, and most datasets record only where cinnamon was bought.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cicero N, Gervasi T, Durazzo A, Lucarini M, Macrì A, Nava V, Giarratana F, Tardugno R, Vadalà R, Santini A · →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-foods-made-with-cinnamon-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="do-foods-made-with-cinnamon-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Do foods made with cinnamon also contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do foods made with cinnamon also contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

They can carry the cinnamon’s metals: in the 2023 outbreak, apple cinnamon pouches held 1,900–5,800 µg/kg lead because of adulterated cinnamon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Napier MD, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Childhood Lead Exposure Linked to Apple Cinnamon Fruit Puree Pouches — North Carolina, June 2023–January 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study in the ledger measured an ordinary cinnamon and the food made with it together.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-levels-in-cinnamon-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-levels-in-cinnamon-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the levels in cinnamon mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the levels in cinnamon mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Cinnamon is eaten in small amounts, about 1.8 mg per kilogram of body weight a day for adult eaters in United States data, but children under seven eat two to five times more per kilogram.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bureau of Toxic Substance Assessment, Center for Environmental Health, New York State Department of Health · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance">Technical Support Document for Derivation of Health-Based Guidance Values for Metals in Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">New York State Department of Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No source in the ledger estimated cinnamon’s share of lead intake, and adulterated cinnamon caused the 2023 outbreak with 566 reported cases of elevated blood lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-cinnamon" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-cinnamon" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, mostly for lead: the EU allows 2.0 mg/kg in bark spices, Codex 2.5 mg/kg, China 3.0 mg/kg for cassia bark and Vietnam 2.0 mg/kg for spices.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">National Health Commission, State Administration for Market Regulation · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants">GB 2762-2025: National Food Safety Standard — Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">National Food Safety Standard of the People&#39;s Republic of China</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Vietnam Ministry of Health · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT National technical regulation on the safety limits of heavy metal contamination in food (English)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Circular No. 02/2011/TT-BYT, QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Vietnam also limits cadmium (1.0 mg/kg) and mercury (0.05 mg/kg) in spices.<sup class="cite">[[sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Vietnam Ministry of Health · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT National technical regulation on the safety limits of heavy metal contamination in food (English)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Circular No. 02/2011/TT-BYT, QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-washing-or-processing-remove-heavy-metals-from-cinnamon" data-anchor="can-washing-or-processing-remove-heavy-metals-from-cinnamon" data-question="Can washing or processing remove heavy metals from cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can washing or processing remove heavy metals from cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only partly, and not reliably: across 23 spices, unwashed portions held on average 7% more lead and 14% more cadmium than washed portions.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No method removes lead chromate from adulterated cinnamon; lots must be tested and rejected.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">LHAAC · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Coordinated Sampling Project 41: Microbial and Heavy Metal Detections in Herbs and Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Local Health Authorities Analytical Committee, Edith Cowan University</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-the-chromium-in-cinnamon-the-toxic-hexavalent-form" data-anchor="is-the-chromium-in-cinnamon-the-toxic-hexavalent-form" data-question="Is the chromium in cinnamon the toxic hexavalent form?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is the chromium in cinnamon the toxic hexavalent form?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Surveys measure total chromium, and no source in the ledger measured hexavalent chromium in cinnamon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-chromium-contam-2014|20]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-chromium-contam-2014">Scientific Opinion on the risks to public health related to the presence of chromium in food and drinking water</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3595</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-chromium-contam-2014">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Lead chromate contains hexavalent chromium, which is why FDA flagged chromium in the outbreak cinnamon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-cinnamon-sticks-lower-in-metals-than-ground-cinnamon" data-anchor="are-cinnamon-sticks-lower-in-metals-than-ground-cinnamon" data-question="Are cinnamon sticks lower in metals than ground cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are cinnamon sticks lower in metals than ground cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, yes in GEMS/Food: sticks had a median of 90 µg/kg against 560 µg/kg for ground cinnamon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For chromium the one paired submission found the opposite.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-ceylon-cinnamon-safer-than-cassia" data-anchor="is-ceylon-cinnamon-safer-than-cassia" data-question="Is Ceylon cinnamon safer than cassia?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is Ceylon cinnamon safer than cassia?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, C. verum-labelled cinnamon measured lower on average in monitoring data, but the labels were not verified and individual C. verum products reached 7,000 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No source in the ledger compared the two species directly under one method.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-does-cinnamon-contamination-affect-children" data-anchor="how-does-cinnamon-contamination-affect-children" data-question="How does cinnamon contamination affect children?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How does cinnamon contamination affect children?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Children under seven eat 4.1–9.1 mg of cinnamon per kilogram of body weight a day among eaters in United States data, more than adults.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bureau of Toxic Substance Assessment, Center for Environmental Health, New York State Department of Health · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance">Technical Support Document for Derivation of Health-Based Guidance Values for Metals in Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">New York State Department of Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The 2023 outbreak affected mostly young children who ate apple cinnamon pouches.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J ·
