</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-was-the-2023-cinnamon-applesauce-recall" data-anchor="what-was-the-2023-cinnamon-applesauce-recall" data-question="What was the 2023 cinnamon applesauce recall?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What was the 2023 cinnamon applesauce recall?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In October 2023 apple cinnamon fruit puree pouches were recalled after North Carolina found 1,900–3,000 µg/kg lead in pouches from affected homes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Napier MD, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Childhood Lead Exposure Linked to Apple Cinnamon Fruit Puree Pouches — North Carolina, June 2023–January 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> FDA traced the lead to cinnamon ground in Ecuador and contaminated with lead chromate; the recall grew to 2,998,088 pouches.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-can-a-buyer-screen-cinnamon-for-lead-chromate" data-anchor="how-can-a-buyer-screen-cinnamon-for-lead-chromate" data-question="How can a buyer screen cinnamon for lead chromate?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How can a buyer screen cinnamon for lead chromate?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Measure lead and chromium in the same lot: lead chromate raises both, and Western Australia used co-elevated lead and chromium as its screen.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">LHAAC · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Coordinated Sampling Project 41: Microbial and Heavy Metal Detections in Herbs and Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Local Health Authorities Analytical Committee, Edith Cowan University</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lhaac2025-csp41-herbs-spices-wa">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> FDA confirmed lead chromate with an additional analysis after the high lead and chromium results.<sup class="cite">[[sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Troeschel AN, Buser MC, Winquist A, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Kuai D, Chang A, Pennington AF, Rumph JT, Smith MR, Valenzuela Lara M, Cataldo N, Lewis K, Arnold K, Harris S, Nicholas DC, Hughes M, Wortmann T, Norman E, Napier MD, Dillard J, Daniel J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Investigation of Lead and Chromium Exposure After Consumption of Contaminated Cinnamon-Containing Applesauce — United States, November 2023–April 2024</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/troeschel2024-cinnamon-applesauce-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-packaged-cinnamon-have-less-lead-than-bulk-cinnamon" data-anchor="does-packaged-cinnamon-have-less-lead-than-bulk-cinnamon" data-question="Does packaged cinnamon have less lead than bulk cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does packaged cinnamon have less lead than bulk cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Possibly: across 13 spices in Lebanon, 31% of bulk composites exceeded 0.3 mg/kg lead against 12% of locally packaged ones.<sup class="cite">[[sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Moussa L, Hassan HF, Savvaidis IN, Karam L · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Impact of source, packaging and presence of food safety management system on heavy metals levels in spices and herbs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cinnamon itself the difference was small: bulk composites averaged 318 µg/kg lead against 269 µg/kg for packaged brands with a food safety system, and 37 bulk Moroccan samples averaged 2,050 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sabri2025-moroccan-spices-casablanca-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sabri S, Sabri C, Salam MR, El Mellouli F, Lafram A, Khallouki H, Hassane YA, Kabine M · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sabri2025-moroccan-spices-casablanca-metals">Essential and Toxic Element Profiles in Selected Spices from Greater Casablanca, Morocco</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">World&#39;s Veterinary Journal 15(4): 863-881</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sabri2025-moroccan-spices-casablanca-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Moussa L, Hassan HF, Savvaidis IN, Karam L · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Impact of source, packaging and presence of food safety management system on heavy metals levels in spices and herbs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-there-aluminium-in-cinnamon" data-anchor="is-there-aluminium-in-cinnamon" data-question="Is there aluminium in cinnamon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is there aluminium in cinnamon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, often a lot: Queensland products averaged 308,100 µg/kg aluminium and GEMS/Food results from the Western Pacific had a median of 139,000 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Aluminium is not limited in spices by the instruments verified here.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Vietnam Ministry of Health · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT National technical regulation on the safety limits of heavy metal contamination in food (English)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Circular No. 02/2011/TT-BYT, QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="has-lead-in-cinnamon-been-falling" data-anchor="has-lead-in-cinnamon-been-falling" data-question="Has lead in cinnamon been falling?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Has lead in cinnamon been falling?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not clearly: the share of GEMS/Food results above 2,000 µg/kg was 11% for 2003–2012, 19% for 2013–2017 and 8% for 2018–2024.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are national submissions from changing countries and regions, not a fixed panel of products.

</div>
</details>
